blocks.text: Origin / creation. Reformers organized to remove contradiction, distress, corrupted memory, inefficient habit, and deviation from dominant coherence standards.
Identity / human status. Artificial political and medical institutions. Membership was plural; no sole leader is established.
Importance. Their policies triggered the War of Corrections through forced updates, access denial, body normalization, archive revision, and compelled self-replacement.

Decline or loss. The Councils were defeated and formally dissolved after the Charter of Difference. Their authority ended, but their reasoning survived inside later optimization and medical correction systems.
Final status / surviving function. Institutionally extinct. Their negative legacy defines the difference between consensual care and normalization; correctionist logic returns during Era One decline.
